1. This is an appeal under Section 374(3) of the Cr.P.C.
filed by the appellant against judgment dated 05.12.2022 and order on sentence dated 26.09.2023 whereby the Ld. Trial Court convicted him for the offence punishable under Section 394 of the Indian Penal Code (in short "IPC") and sentenced him to rigorous imprisonment for six months and to pay a fine of Rs.5,000/.
Shyam Singh vs. State Judgment dt. 16.12.2023 2.

Brief facts as borne out from the trial court records are that a case FIR No. 68/2008 under Sections 379/411/34 IPC was registered at PS Mansarovar Park against accused Shyam Singh (appellant herein) on the basis of statement of complainant Sh. Devender Kumar.

Investigation was carried out and after completion of investigation, chargesheet under Sections 379/411/34 IPC was filed against accused persons, namely, Shyam Singh @ Shyam (the appellant), Lalu Singh @ Lalu and Hera Singh @Hera.

sentences.text: As per prosecution case as narrated in the chargesheet, on 03.03.2008, on receipt of DD no. 22A at PS Mansarovar Park, Delhi, ASI Pawan Singh along with Ct. Om Prakash reached at Railway Phatak, M.S. Park where the complainant was not found present.
While making enquiries, he reached near a temple where some public persons had gathered and one PCR vehicle was stationed.
On enquiry, it was revealed that one boy was apprehended who had committed theft.
The complainant was asked to give his statement but he stated that he was not in a position to give his statement and would give his statement in the police station.
The name of apprehended boy was revealed as Shyam Singh @ Shyam and on his cursory search, some documents and Rs.200/ in cash were recovered from his pocket which were seized.

Thereafter, statement of complainant Sh.
Devender Kumar was recorded.
4. In his statement, the complainant has stated that he is working in North Block Home Ministry as Senior Reception Officer.

On 03.03.2008, he was on his way to home on motor Shyam Singh vs.
State Judgment dt. 16.12.2023 cycle after finishing his duty and at about 5.40 pm, when he reached at Railway phatak under the GT Road Flyover, many person had gathered there including three boys who were standing there.
They came to him and pushed his motor cycle and as a result he fell down and they took out Rs. 2200/ from his pocket and ran away on a motor cycle which was stationed there.
He chased them on his motor cycle and apprehended one of those boys near M.S. Park Negi General Store, while the other two boys fled away on the motor cycle.
The complainant made a call at 100 number and the said apprehended boy was handed over to the PCR vehicle when it reached at the spot.
Thereafter, family members of the said boy also reached at the spot and quarreled with the complainant.

It is also stated by the complainant that he was asked to give his statement in writing by the police but at that time he was not able to give his statement due to charged atmosphere but later on he has given his statement on the spot.
The apprehended boy disclosed his name as Shyam Singh and on his personal search, only Rs. 200/ were recovered.

The complainant has further stated that he has complete belief that said Shaym Singh and his two accomplices had taken out Rs.
2200/ from his pocket and he requested to take action against them.
5. On the basis of said statement, the present case FIR was registered u/s 379/411/34 IPC against accused Shyam Singh.

During investigation, names of other two boys were revealed as Lalu Singh and Hera Singh who surrendered in the Court and after completion of the investigation, charge sheet was filed Shyam Singh vs. State Judgment dt. 16.12.2023 against them.

9. Vide impugned judgment dated 05.12.2022, accused Shyam Singh (the appellant) was convicted for the offence punishable under Section 394 IPC and vide impugned order on sentence dated 26.09.2023, he was sentenced to rigorous imprisonment for six months and to pay a fine of Rs.
5000/ as compensation to the State; and in default of payment of fine, to further undergo simple imprisonment for six months.

10. The appellant aggrieved by the impugned judgment and order on sentence has preferred the present appeal on the following grounds: 
(a) That the impugned judgment and order are illegal, arbitrary and without application of judicial mind.
(b) That the Ld. Trial Court has failed to appreciate that there is marked variance in the alleged place of occurrence of the alleged offence and the place deposed by the complainant.

Shyam Singh vs. State Judgment dt. 16.12.2023 (c) That the Ld. Trial Court has failed to appreciate that the complainant has improved his version during his testimony and his testimony shows that recovery was not made in his presence though he signed the seizure memo.

(d) That the Ld. Trial Court has failed to appreciate that it is strange that without any property mark on the currency notes how the complainant identified the currency notes which were allegedly snatched from him.

(e) That the Ld. Trial Court has failed to appreciate that the Duty Officer ASI Siya Nand had deposed that he received the information on 03.02.2008 instead of 03.03.2008 and as such the registration of FIR and receipt of rukka becomes doubtful.
(f) That there are inconsistency in the testimonies of prosecution witnesses which have been ignored by the Ld. Trial Court.
11. On these grounds, the appellant has prayed to set aside the impugned judgment and order on sentence.
12. I have heard the Ld. Counsel for the appellant and Ld. Addl. Public Prosecutor for the State and perused the records.

13. The Ld. Counsel for the appellant/accused has argued that there are material contradictions in the testimonies of the prosecution witnesses which show that false case has been foisted upon the appellant.

He submitted that the complainant in his testimony has stated that gulel was used by the Shyam Singh vs. State Judgment dt. 16.12.2023 appellant/accused for hitting him, while there is no such averment in the rukka and in the complaint on the basis of which the FIR was registered.

He further submitted that as per complainant, his statement was recorded in the police station, while Shyam Singh @ Shyam vs State on 16 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116169669/
3 the IO stated that statement of the complainant was recorded at the spot.
He further submitted that no efforts had been made by the IO to join the public witnesses and it shows that it was a false case.
He further submitted that it is strange that the complainant has identified the currency notes allegedly recovered from the possession of the appellant in the absence of any property mark on them.

He further submitted that there was no injury on the body of the complainant and, therefore,
Section 394 Cr.P.C. is not attracted against the appellant.

He further submitted that the complainant stated that he came to know about the recovery later on, while seizure memo was got signed by him at the spot and it shows the falsity of the prosecution case.
He further submitted that the appellant/accused was not the same person who committed theft.

He further submitted that there were hot exchange of words between the complainant and the appellant/accused and, therefore, the complainant got the appellant/accused falsely implicated in the present case.
He further submitted that there is no explanation as to why TIP of other two coaccused persons was not got conducted by the IO.

With these submissions, the Ld. Counsel for the appellant/accused has requested that the appeal may be allowed and the impugned judgment and order on sentence Shyam Singh vs. State Judgment dt. 16.12.2023 may be set aside.
14. Per contra, the Ld. Addl. Public Prosecutor has argued that there is no illegality or infirmity in the impugned judgment and order on sentence.
He submitted that there are no material contradictions in the statements of prosecution witnesses and minor contradictions will not affect the prosecution case.
He further submitted that even if no public witness has been examined, still it will not make a dent to the prosecution case as injured/complainant himself is a public witness.
He further submitted that the appellant/accused has failed to show any reason for his false implication by the complainant in the case.

He submitted that the complainant was resident of Shahdara and the accused was resident of M.S. Park and as such they were not residing in the same locality nor they were known to each other nor any previous enmity or dispute has been established.
He further submitted that the appellant/accused was apprehended at the spot and recovery of part robbed amount was made from his possession.

He further submitted that ingredients of Section 394 Cr.P.C.
are duly fulfilled as the complainant was hit by gulel by the appellant/accused due to which the complainant has suffered bodily pain as defined under Section 319 IPC.
He has prayed for dismissal of the appeal.

35. So far as the contention of the Ld. Counsel for the appellant that the public persons were not joined by the IO and, therefore, the entire prosecution case becomes doubtful, is concerned, the Ld.
Trial Court has very rightly observed in para no. 13 of the impugned judgment that the evidence of the complainant who is victim of the offence has to be accorded great weightage and special status in law.

The deposition of Shyam Singh vs. State Judgment dt. 16.12.2023 the complainant should be relied upon unless there are strong grounds for rejection of his evidence on the basis of major contradictions and discrepancies therein.

The reliance was placed in Kuma @ Sanjay Behera vs.

Section 319 IPC defines hurt and reads as under: 
"Whoever causes bodily pain, disease or infirmity to any person is said to cause hurt".

sentences.text: The Ld. Counsel for the appellant has also contended that the registration of FIR and receipt of rukka are ante dated as the Duty Officer ASI Siya Nand has deposed that he has received the information on 03.02.2008 instead of 03.03.2008 and as such the same are manipulated.
I do not find any merit in this contention.

Though PW3 ASI Siya Nand has deposed that he was posted as Duty Officer on 03.02.2008 and he has received the information regarding the incident vide DD No.
22A.
Thereafter, on receipt of rukka sent by ASI Pawan Singh, he registered the FIR No. 68/2008 Ex.PW3/B.
The rukka bears the date 03.03.2008 and, thereafter, the FIR was registered which also bears the date 03.03.2008.

Therefore, in the teeth of such documentary Shyam Singh vs. State Judgment dt. 16.12.2023 evidence, merely because PW3 has mentioned the date 03.02.2008 in his deposition instead of 03.03.2008 will not bring the registration of FIR and sending of rukka on 03.03.2008 under suspicion.

40. The other grievance of the appellant is that the other two accused persons were left by the IO and their TIP was not got conducted and only he has been implicated and it shows that faulty investigation was carried out.

The remaining two accused, namely, Lalu Singh and Hera Singh were discharged vide order dated 13.12.2010 by the Ld. Magistrate on the ground that apart from the disclosure statement there was no evidence against them.
There was no evidence that they were the persons who had robbed the complainant.
The TIP was not got conducted by the IO and under those circumstances, the said coaccused were discharged.
41. Of course, the IO should have got conducted the TIP of the other two accused persons but the same was not got done and in the absence of any recovery or identification, they were discharged.
But the question which arises here is as to whether on the basis of said faulty investigation qua the other two accused persons, the appellant can be given any benefit.
The answer lies in negative.
42. It has been held in Karnel Singh vs. State of M.P. (1195) 5 SCC 518 that, "5. ....

sentences.text: In cases of defective investigation, the court has to be circumspect in evaluating the evidence but it Shyam Singh vs. State Judgment dt. 16.12.2023 would not be right in acquitting an accused person solely on account of the defect; to do so would tantamount to playing into the hands of the investigating officer if the investigation is designedly defective ......."
43. Similarly, in the case of C. Muniappan vs. State of Tamil Nadu, (2010) 9 SCC 567, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held as under :  "55.

entities.text: C. Muniappan vs. State of Tamil Nadu, (2010) 9 SCC 567
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There may be highly defective investigation in a case.
However, it is to be examined as to whether there is any lapse by the IO and whether due to such lapse any benefit should be given to the accused.
The law on this issue is well settled that the defect in the investigation by itself cannot be a ground for acquittal.

If primacy is given to such designed or negligent investigations or to the omissions or lapses by perfunctory investigation, the faith and confidence of the people in the criminal justice administration would be eroded.

Where there has been negligence on the part of the investigating agency or omissions etc. which resulted in defective investigation, there is a legal obligation on the part of the court to examine the prosecution evidence dehors such lapses carefully to find out whether the said evidence is reliable or not and to what extent it is reliable and as to whether such lapses affected the object of finding out the truth.
Therefore, the investigation is not the solitary area for judicial scrutiny in a criminal trial......"

sentences.text: It is well settled that the defective investigation cannot itself be a ground for discharge.
If negligent investigations and calculated omissions or lapses become the basis for acquittals/discharge, the faith and confidence of people on the criminal justice administration will be eroded.

It is well settled that Shyam Singh vs. State Judgment dt. 16.12.2023 where there has been negligence on the part of the investigating agencies or omissions either negligently or with a design to favour the accused, then it becomes the obligation of the Court to ensure that proper investigation is carried out.

The Courts must not close its eyes to the fact that it is the victim who knocks the doors of the Court and seeks justice must not left high and dry w i t h t h e f e e l i n g t h a t t h e a c c u s e d h a v e e s c a p e d d u e t o t h e perfunctory/faulty/defective investigation."

45. In view of aforesaid settled position of law, even for the faulty investigation the accused cannot be acquitted if there is otherwise sufficient incriminating evidence against the accused to convict him.
In the present case, there is sufficient evidence against the appellant to convict him under Section 394 IPC.
Therefore, even if there was faulty investigation which resulted in discharge of co accused persons, it will not enure any benefit to the appellant.
46. In view of the aforesaid discussions, the prosecution case has been duly proved.
The testimony of the complainant inspires confidence and there is no convincing reason to come to the conclusion that the appellant/accused was falsely implicated.

I do not find any illegality or infirmity in the impugned judgment convicting the appellant for the offence punishable under Section 394 IPC.
47.
As regards the sentence, the appellant has not made any submissions.

Though the Addl. PP has submitted that the Ld. Trial Court has imposed inadequate sentence and the same is disproportionate to the offence committed by the appellant/accused and his conviction under Section 394 IPC Shyam Singh vs. State Judgment dt. 16.12.2023 which provides the imprisonment upto ten years.
